scope: Proposition 4.1 of the manuscript “Electromagnetic tails and the Kerr–Newman Penrose inequality” (preprints/Electromagnetic-tails-and-the-Kerr-Newman-Penrose-inequality-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ffdf93f60ad3ab23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all sufficiently large L, uniformly for 0 ≤ s ≤ 1, the data constructed in Sections 2 and 3 are smooth source-free electrovacuum data on Ω = {x ∈ R3 : r ≥ 1}, S = {r = 1}, 10 with trg K = 0. The metric is complete with its boundary included, has one asymptotically flat end, and satisfies gij − δij = O4(r−1 ), Kij = O3(r−3 ), Ei , Bi = O3(r−2 ). (4.1) The standard effective U(1) action preserves all the data and S, and µ and |Jcon|g are integrable. With the normal toward the end, S is a future MOTS, and no compact smooth embedded enclosing surface in int Ω, possibly disconnected, has everywhere nonpositive future outward expansion. Every enclosing cut in the sense of Section 1 has area at least A = Areag(S). Moreover, for a constant CA independent of s, L, 64π ≤ A ≤ 64π + CA s2 L2 , A = 64π + O(s2 /L2 ), (4.2) and A(s, L) is continuous in s for fixed L.
